title: Godot crashes when undoing a deleted animation point on a `BlendSpace1D` node
body:
### Tested versions - Reproducible: 4.7 dev 4, 4.7 beta 1 and latest master - Not reproducible: 4.7 dev 2 ### System information Godot v4.7.dev (e93f67140) - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Intel(R) Arc(TM) B580 Graphics (Intel Corporation; 32.0.101.8735) - AMD Ryzen 5 3600 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.91 GiB memory ### Issue description Originally reported here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/118945#issuecomment-4319995992 Regression from: #117277 When you delete the first created animation point inside a `BlendeSpace1D` node that contain two or more points, attempting to undo the deletation crashes the engine. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d76e0f6c-8220-4855-b82c-dcd9d86c4459

If you do all the steps, except connecting the `BlendSpace1D` node with the `Output` node, only the `ERROR: Condition "E.name.is_empty()" is true. Continuing.` will appear, but at the moment you connect the nodes, the editor will crash with the same backtrace. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a `Node3D` 2. Create an `AnimationPlayer` node 3. Create an animation, you can let the animation empty 4. Create an `AnimationTree` node 5. On the `AnimationTree` node, set the `Anim Player` property to the created `AnimationPlayer` node 6. On `Tree Root` property, create an `AnimationNodeBlendTree` resource 7. Create a `BlendSpace1D` node and connect to the `Output` node 8. Click on the `Open Editor` button on the `BlendSpace1D` node 9. Add two animations points 10. Delete the first point added (only crash deleting the first one) 11. Press `Ctrl + Z` to undo 12. Crash ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [blend-space-crash.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27105567/blend-space-crash.zip)
